description: CR-001 remainder and recovery: Windows lifecycle script audit and mutex, 6a shutdown blocker (ADR-0021), 6b User32 1074 task, bootstrap -Uninstall/-Shortcuts and doctor checks, the root lifecycle helper behind Telegram /down and /up, full-stack crash safety incl. runner and Hermes, and ossctl backup/restore with Windows wrappers. Depends on FEAT-006 and FEAT-007. Plan: docs/PLAN.md (Lifecycle remainder, crash safety, backup and restore). Requirement rows: docs/TRACEABILITY.md.
steps: Item 39: Windows lifecycle scripts audit (CR-001 5; rows DES-FR-17, CR1-5a). `status.ps1` shows every CR-001 field (lifecycle, kill, dry-run, stages, approvals, outbox, last poll + reconnects, last shutdown type, task states, egress mode, Hermes tier); `down.ps1`/`up.ps1` serialise on `Local\ossbot-lifecycle` and log to `.ossbot-local\lifecycle.log`; live down → status → up recorded. Carried detail from the interrupted planner draft (FEAT numbers remapped; DESIGN revision 5 and the item text above win on any conflict, e.g. no Pillow in the gatekeeper, streaming via drafts, decision services from FEAT-005): Draft item 21: CR-001 §5 audit of scripts/up.ps1, scripts/down.ps1, scripts/status.ps1 and fix the gaps: status.ps1 shows on one screen lifecycle, kill, dry-run, running stages, pending approvals, outbox depth, last successful Telegram poll + reconnects, last shutdown type (graceful/hook/unclean from the boot-gate marker), the autostart/blocker/hook task states; down.ps1 and up.ps1 serialise on a per-user named mutex 'Local\ossbot-lifecycle' (decision: a second caller - e.g. 6a and 6b firing during the same shutdown - waits up to its own timeout, then exits 0 if the distro is already stopped), log to d:\Work\autonomous-oss-contributor\.ossbot-local\lifecycle.log, and keep PowerShell 5.1 compatibility (use the Invoke-OssWsl helpers). Live, non-destructive: down.ps1 -Timeout 10 -> status.ps1 -> up.ps1 -> status.ps1, record times.

Item 40: 6a shutdown blocker (rows DES-AC-32, DES-V-31, CR1-6a). Research first and record a new ADR (`docs/adr/0021-windows-shutdown-hooks.md`): `WM_QUERYENDSESSION`, `ShutdownBlockReasonCreate/Destroy`, hidden/off-screen windows, Fast Startup. `scripts/windows/ossbot-shutdown-blocker.ps1` (PowerShell 5.1, C# compiled at runtime from repo source, single instance, log in `.ossbot-local\`), started by `ossbot-autostart`; non-destructive `tests/system/test_shutdown_blocker.ps1`. The real shutdown test happens in item 57. Carried detail from the interrupted planner draft (FEAT numbers remapped; DESIGN revision 5 and the item text above win on any conflict, e.g. no Pillow in the gatekeeper, streaming via drafts, decision services from FEAT-005): Draft item 22: 6a shutdown blocker. Research first (record in a new docs/adr/0021-windows-shutdown-hooks.md): WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION, ShutdownBlockReasonCreate/Destroy requirements (top-level window, hidden or off-screen behaviour), the 5 s/'apps preventing shutdown' UI on Windows 11 26100, Fast Startup (HiberbootEnabled, read-only registry check) and whether WM_QUERYENDSESSION arrives on 'Shut down' with Fast Startup. Implement scripts/windows/ossbot-shutdown-blocker.ps1 (PowerShell 5.1, Add-Type C# compiled at runtime from source in the repo, no binary checked in, no copies to AppData): a top-level WinForms window (not shown in the taskbar; off-screen or hidden per the research) overriding WndProc; on WM_QUERYENDSESSION it calls ShutdownBlockReasonCreate('ossbot: stopping safely…'), runs scripts\down.ps1 -Timeout 90 (hard cap 90 + 90 s), then ShutdownBlockReasonDestroy and returns TRUE; single instance via a named mutex; logs to .ossbot-local\shutdown-blocker.log. Started at logon as a second action of the existing ossbot-autostart task (CR-001 wording) with ExecutionTimeLimit PT0S so Task Scheduler never kills it; kill.ps1 -Hard keeps disabling the task. Non-destructive live test tests\system\test_shutdown_blocker.ps1: start the blocker, find its window, SendMessage(WM_QUERYENDSESSION) to it, assert ShutdownBlockReasonQuery shows the reason while down runs, the distro ends stopped with shutdown type graceful, the reason is destroyed afterwards; then up.ps1.

Item 41: 6b event task and bootstrap install/uninstall (rows DES-NFR-3, CR1-5d, CR1-6b, CR1-6d). `ossbot-shutdown-hook` (System/User32 1074 only, non-elevated, `down.ps1 -Timeout 20 -Kind hook`, PT2M limit), SpiralPool BSD-3 credit (and notice if code is adapted); `bootstrap.ps1` phase `shutdownhooks`, `-Uninstall`, optional `-Shortcuts`; `ossctl.ps1 doctor` checks; `Start-ScheduledTask` live test. Carried detail from the interrupted planner draft (FEAT numbers remapped; DESIGN revision 5 and the item text above win on any conflict, e.g. no Pillow in the gatekeeper, streaming via drafts, decision services from FEAT-005): Draft item 23: 6b event-triggered task 'ossbot-shutdown-hook' modelled on SpiralPool scripts/windows/wsl2-shutdown-hook.ps1 (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright (c) 2026 Spiral Pool Contributors): per-user, non-elevated (RunLevel Limited, the logged-on user), trigger = event subscription System log, Provider User32, EventID 1074 only (NOT Kernel-Power 42 or any sleep event, unlike SpiralPool), action powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File d:\Work\autonomous-oss-contributor\scripts\down.ps1 -Timeout 20 -Kind hook with ExecutionTimeLimit PT2M; script and log stay in the repo (no %APPDATA% helper copy, unlike SpiralPool). Verify a non-admin user can register a System-log event trigger on 26100; if not, record WARN in doctor and the ADR. If any SpiralPool code is adapted, keep its SPDX/copyright header in the adapted file and add a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry with the BSD-3 text; credit it in the shutdown-hooks ADR either way. Document that Windows does not wait for scheduled tasks (best effort). bootstrap.ps1: new phase 'shutdownhooks' installs 6a (autostart second action) and 6b, '-Uninstall' (new switch, reusing scripts\uninstall-host.ps1 logic) removes them and the autostart task, optional '-Shortcuts' creates Start-menu shortcuts 'ossbot Up/Down/Status/Kill' (off by default). ossctl.ps1 doctor checks the blocker process is running, the autostart second action and the hook task trigger XML match. Non-destructive live test: Start-ScheduledTask ossbot-shutdown-hook -> distro stops with shutdown type 'hook' -> up.ps1.

Item 42: Telegram lifecycle root helper and full-stack crash safety (rows DES-AC-31, DES-AC-32, CR1-5c, CR1-6c2). `scripts/bin/ossbot-lifecycle` + `systemd/ossbot-lifecycle.{path,service}` consuming a gatekeeper-written lifecycle request (`down` scope workers, `up`; regular file ≤ 4 KiB, ≤ 5 min old, always consumed, `up` refused while killed); `POST /v1/control/lifecycle-request` (human). `tests/system/test_crash_safety.sh` covers gatekeeper, sandboxd, dockerfilter, runner and Hermes; `test_lifecycle.sh` gains the workers-down case.

Item 43: Backup and restore, then commit FEAT-008 (§18.8; rows DES-FR-15, DES-NFR-10, DES-AC-22, DES-V-26, ADR-0016, CHAT-18). `ctl/{backup,restore}.py`, `scripts/{backup,restore}.ps1`, `ossbot-backup.{service,timer}` (installed disabled), age pinned; include list = §18.8 + Hermes state, active skills, feature stores, `config/telegram.yaml`, chat-attachment policy (attachments excluded by default); restore leaves killed + dry-run ON with all decision services invalidated; `tests/unit/ctl/{test_backup,test_restore}.py`, `tests/system/test_backup_roundtrip.sh`. Carried detail from the interrupted planner draft (FEAT numbers remapped; DESIGN revision 5 and the item text above win on any conflict, e.g. no Pillow in the gatekeeper, streaming via drafts, decision services from FEAT-005): Draft item 24: crash safety and backup/restore. Run the full-stack SIGKILL e2e: tests/system/test_crash_safety.sh now covers gatekeeper, sandboxd, dockerfilter, runner (FEAT-006) and hermes (add it: SIGKILL ossbot-hermes mid-relay -> restart, relay re-gated by probe + surface check). Backup (DESIGN §18.8, ADR-0016): verify §23 item 26 (age release, sha256, 'age -d -i -' from stdin), pin age in config/versions.lock.yaml, install it in the apt-base step; src/ossbot/ctl/{backup.py,restore.py} (pause/checkpoint, SQLite online backup, audit verify on the copy, MANIFEST with sha256 per file, age-encrypted to profile.backup.age_recipients (refuse when empty), retention 8 in the gitignored d:\Work\autonomous-oss-contributor\backups\, include list = §18.8 + the Hermes state, active skills, feature stores and chat-attachment layout from the FEAT-007/009 findings; restore moves current state aside, forces killed + dry-run ON, invalidates approvals, re-applies chattr +a); ossctl 'backup [now]', 'backup schedule on|off', 'restore <archive>'; scripts/{backup.ps1,restore.ps1}; systemd/ossbot-backup.{service,timer} installed disabled. Tests: tests/unit/ctl/{test_backup.py,test_restore.py}, tests/system/test_backup_roundtrip.sh (in-place AC 22: audit verify passes, Hermes memory files identical, restored state killed + dry-run ON; the test resumes the system afterwards and uses a throwaway age identity under /root/.cache/ossbot-test, never the owner's).
acceptance_criteria: status.ps1 shows every CR-001 §5 field; down/up serialise; the live down -> status -> up cycle is recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md

tests\system\test_shutdown_blocker.ps1 passes (WM_QUERYENDSESSION -> block reason set -> graceful down -> reason destroyed); Start-ScheduledTask ossbot-shutdown-hook brings the distro down with shutdown type 'hook'; bootstrap installs both, bootstrap -Uninstall removes both, ossctl.ps1 doctor checks both; ADR-0021 records the research and credits SpiralPool
Telegram /down (scope workers) and /up work through the root lifecycle helper: runner, Hermes and sandboxd stop, the gatekeeper keeps answering; tests/system/test_lifecycle.sh passes the workers case

DEV pytest -m unit tests/unit/ctl passes (manifest covers every included item, archive always encrypted, tampered manifest refused, restore leaves killed + dry-run ON with approvals invalidated); tests/system/test_backup_roundtrip.sh passes; the include list covers Hermes state, active skills, feature stores and config/telegram.yaml; restore invalidates every decision service
ruff, mypy, lint-imports, shellcheck clean; PowerShell scripts parse under 5.1; TRACEABILITY rows updated; git status --porcelain empty after the commit

DEV ruff check src tests ; DEV ruff format --check src tests ; DEV mypy ; DEV lint-imports

Decisions within DESIGN revision 5 (no behaviour beyond it): the blocker's down uses kind graceful as DESIGN 13.5 names it (the plan text said -Kind blocker; down.ps1 -Caller blocker is logged instead); a hook down yields 3 s to a running blocker so the 90 s path normally takes the mutex first; restore uses a soft kill and starts the gatekeeper and proxy again so /resume on Telegram works (DESIGN 18.8 step 5 wording); the backup lifts only its own pause through ossbot-resume --paused-only, whose resume.log line is no P1-7 kill evidence (DESIGN 18.8 step 1 note, ADR-0016 addendum); Hermes include list = DESIGN's '.hermes minus code and caches' as an exclude list (a superset of the FEAT-007 list; the live layout has cron, kanban, shared-state and state dirs too); config/telegram.yaml is included when present.
Found live and fixed: (1) Hermes SIGKILLed mid-relay gave an uncaught httpx.RemoteProtocolError (HTTP 500, chat turn left streaming): every httpx TransportError is HermesUnavailable now (gatekeeper/chat/hermes_api.py, unit test). (2) A burst of refused lifecycle requests tripped systemd's start limit and left ossbot-lifecycle.path failed: StartLimitIntervalSec=0 (each run consumes its request first). (3) The first restore wrote the drvfs config/profile.yaml as root 0600: the gatekeeper could not read it, restart loop, the watchdog paused (gatekeeper_unhealthy) and reconcile raised 'kill flag missing; use /resume' on every tick (about 14 alert FYIs to the owner) until an offline resume; the recorded owner and mode are applied on drvfs too now, the live file was put back to ossadmin:osscfg 0775 and the system resumed. (4) ossbot-kill reported PARTIAL because a killed container is still listed for < 0.5 s: it waits up to 10 s now. (5) After a reboot while killed the Hermes probe socket stayed down after a resume: ossbot-resume starts it. test_kill case 5 bound 40 -> 45 s (wsl --terminate takes 10.1 s now) and case 2 polls /status.

Dry-run stayed ON, no GitHub write, Telegram only to the owner through product code (lifecycle/kill/pause FYIs, the alerts of fix (3)), no secret read or printed by hand (backups ran without secrets and with a throwaway identity). Open rows (all with later owners): CR1-6a, CR1-6b, DES-V-31, DES-AC-32 real-restart parts -> FEAT-011 item 57 (added to its Rows in phase2-build-plan.md and FEAT-011.json); CR1-5c and DES-AC-31 Telegram /drain /undrain /down /up -> FEAT-009 item 47 (the backend is POST /v1/control/lifecycle-request); DES-FR-17 Telegram part -> FEAT-009; DES-FR-15 and DES-NFR-10 SETUP.md runbook -> FEAT-011 item 54.
For FEAT-011 (SETUP.md and item 57): Daily use: scripts\up.ps1, down.ps1 [-Timeout S] [-All], status.ps1 [-Json] (one screen; every field also with the distro stopped), kill.ps1 [-Hard], resume.ps1; optional bootstrap.ps1 -Shortcuts (Start-menu 'ossbot Up/Down/Status/Kill', off by default; Kill is a full kill without a prompt). Shutdown hooks: installed by bootstrap (phases autostart and shutdownhooks); at shutdown/restart/sign-out Windows may show 'ossbot: stopping safely...' for up to ~3 min (the user may pick 'Shut down anyway'); the 6b task is best effort; logs .ossbot-local\shutdown-blocker.log and lifecycle.log; status.ps1 'last shutdown' graceful (6a or down.ps1), hook (6b) or unclean; Fast Startup is on here and needs no change. Item 57 real restart: ask the user (send_message warning) to restart once normally, then check shutdown-blocker.log (WM_QUERYENDSESSION line, reason created/destroyed, down.ps1 exit), lifecycle.log (caller=blocker and/or caller=hook, which one got the lock), status.ps1 last shutdown, and whether Windows showed the reason and continued by itself; record in ADR-0021 and close CR1-6a/6b, DES-V-31, DES-AC-32. If a cancelled shutdown leaves ossbot down (WM_ENDSESSION(FALSE) is logged), scripts\up.ps1 brings it back (no automatic up: not in DESIGN; ask the owner if wanted). Uninstall: bootstrap.ps1 -Uninstall [-Only shortcuts,shutdownhooks,autostart,hyperv,wsl] (never the distro, VHD or repo). Backup (SETUP step 6): generate an identity once (e.g. wsl -d ossbot -u root --exec /usr/local/bin/age-keygen, or age-keygen on Windows), keep the AGE-SECRET-KEY file outside the machine (password manager), put only the public key into config/profile.yaml backup.age_recipients (classic age1... or post-quantum age1pq1..., not mixed), reload; scripts\backup.ps1 [-IncludeSecrets] [-IncludeArtifacts] [-IncludeAttachments] writes backups\ossbot-<ts>.tar.age (keep 8; secrets also by policy backup.include_secrets); ossctl backup schedule on|off (weekly Sunday 03:00 timer, disabled by default; with no recipient it fails and writes nothing). Restore: scripts\restore.ps1 -Archive backups\<name> -Identity <path to the identity file> (types RESTORE; the archive must be inside the repo; a passphrase-protected identity needs an unprotected temporary copy because the stdin stream has no terminal for age's prompt); afterwards ossbot is killed (soft) with dry-run ON and every open approval invalidated: run scripts\ossctl.ps1 doctor, then /resume; the replaced state stays in /srv/ossbot/restore-previous-<ts>/ (never pruned automatically; the user may delete old ones); the DB is rolled back to the archive's moment. Fresh-machine DR (AC 22 full form, by the user): bootstrap, then restore (secrets come back only from an archive made with -IncludeSecrets, else setup-secrets.ps1). config/profile.example.yaml already has backup.age_recipients (no new profile key in FEAT-008).
Notes for later FEATs: the reconcile alert 'kill flag missing; use /resume' repeats on every tick while the DB says killed and only a pause flag exists (Phase 1 behaviour; it spammed ~14 FYIs in fix (3)): FEAT-009's notification coalescing (item 47) should cover it. Two /srv/ossbot/restore-previous-* dirs from the live roundtrip runs are kept by design. test_bootstrap_zero.ps1 (updated for the shutdownhooks skip and -Uninstall refusal) needs a throwaway test distro and was not run.
